https://www.politico.eu/article/france-t.text: BRUSSELS — French President Emmanuel Macron said on Saturday that Paris will strengthen its support for Ukraine after Russia’s deadly attacks on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih on Friday. Macron wrote on X that he called Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday following the strikes, which killed 16 and left 130 injured. “I informed President Zelensky that we are stepping up our support with the delivery of interceptors and are continuing our cooperation,” he said. Confirming the phone call during which the pair discussed “first and foremost, the need for air defense,” Zelenskyy also shared on social media that the two leaders had “agreed to accelerate the delivery of the latest French equipment and missiles.” Advertisement Advertisement “Thank you for confirming your readiness to provide licenses for the production of missiles,” wrote the Ukrainian leader. Regarding relations with Washington, Zelenskyy said he and Macron “also discussed the state of diplomatic work with our partners and communication with the team of the President of the United States. We agreed on steps that could open up additional diplomatic opportunities.” Macron, along with his counterparts from Germany and the U.K., are expected to co-host a Coalition of the Willing meeting on Monday to discuss continued support for Ukraine against Russia’s aggression. The meeting will be held in Kyiv, with some leaders — including the French president — dialing in remotely. Around 10 leaders, including European Council President António Costa , are expected to attend in person, reported Le Monde.

https://www.dw.com/en/ex-bosnian-serb-mi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JVaF Mladic was dubbed the 'Butcher of Bosnia' for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre [FILE: June 8, 2021] Image: Jerry Lampen/REUTERS Advertisement Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic, who was serving a life sentence for war crimes committed during Bosnia and Herzegovina's 1992-95 war has died, a United Nations official said. Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday that he died in a prison hospital in the Hague, after suffering several strokes. A family member of Mladic, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the situation, confirmed the reports to the Associated Press and said Mladic's son, Darko Mladic, was on the way to the Hague. The International Criminal Court for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic of charges including crimes against humanity and genocide in 2017, handing him a life sentence. The verdict was confirmed on appeal in 2021. 30 years on: The Srebrenica genocide explained To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Commenting on Mladic's death on Thursday, United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres expressed his support for the war criminal's victims. "The secretary-general stands in solidarity with the victims, survivors and their families who suffered the crimes for which Mr Mladic was found guilty," spokesman Stephane Dujarric told reporters. 'The butcher of Bosnia' Mladic was held responsible for his role in the 1992 to 1995 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including July 1995 massacre of some 8,000 Muslim men and boys at Srebrenica. The slaughter, the worst single atrocity in Europe since World War II, saw him named the "Butcher of Bosnia." Under Mladic's command, Bosnian Serb forces besieged Sarajevo and other towns, operated detention camps for non-Serbs and enemy soldiers, and systematically killed prisoners. Did foreigners pay to shoot civilians during Sarajevo siege? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Former UN rights chief Zeid Ra'ad al Hussein described him as "the epitome of evil" after his conviction. "This is all lies, you are all liars," he shouted when he was sentenced to life in prison in 2017. On Monday, Serbia's justice minister, Nenad Vujic, asked for Mladic to be transferred to a Belgrade military hospital, warning that his death "could come at any time." Srebrenica massacre discredited international community Born in Bosnia in 1942, Mladic was a former Yugoslav army officer who rose to command the Bosnian Serb army during the 1992-95 war. A hardline nationalist, he portrayed the conflict as a historic struggle against Ottoman rule and celebrated the 1995 capture of Srebrenica. After the capture of the city, Mladic ordered the evacuation of women, children and the elderly but said all men of fighting age are taken prisoner. In the following days more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys are systematically butchered by the Bosnian Serb forces and their bodies dumped in mass graves. Mladic was the military face of a brutal trio, led on the political side by ex-Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic and former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic [August 5, 1993] Image: Str/epa/dpa/picture alliance In 2022 The Netherlands apologized for the Dutch peacekeepers' failure to prevent the killings. Mladic himself have never repented. Edited by: Rana Taha Don't let the algorithm hide the news. https://nineoclock.ro/ing-bank-study-two.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Travel often involves costs that Romanians don’t factor in from the start: from exchanging currency on the spot at an unfavorable rate to medical expenses or roadside assistance services paid out of pocket. A study conducted for ING Bank Romania shows that 66% of Romanians have ended up paying more than necessary on a trip due to financial improvisations. Unforeseen costs directly impact your personal budget Some of these unexpected situations result in expenses that must be covered out of pocket while traveling, when they are harder to anticipate and manage. Data from the study* conducted by Frappe Digital for ING Bank shows that 30% of respondents paid for medical procedures or treatments not covered by insurance, and 10% incurred costs for unplanned roadside assistance. For parents, the pressure can be even greater: when it comes to these types of costs, they are nearly twice as likely to cover them out of their own pockets. “ When traveling, we often encounter what we call “financial improvisations”, situations where you have to make decisions on the spot, whether it’s about currency exchange, a medical issue, or other unexpected costs. These are moments that are sometimes part of the travel experience and can affect both your budget and the comfort of your vacation. With ING More and ING Extra, we wanted to offer benefits tailored to such situations, so that customers have useful solutions at their fingertips when they travel,” said Roxana Petria, Head of the Daily Banking Tribe at ING Bank Romania. Many Romanians are still caught off guard by currency exchange costs The study shows that currency exchange remains one of the most common financial transactions associated with travel, with more than half of Romanians exchanging currency at least occasionally. At the same time, nearly one in five respondents says that, in the past year, they faced costs they hadn’t anticipated when they needed to exchange currency. The ability to check exchange rates in advance and take advantage of favorable exchange terms can help travelers better manage their travel budget, a need that is also addressed by ING’s checking account packages, which include access to favorable exchange rates. When traveling abroad, payment habits remain divided: 30% choose to pay directly with their card and use automatic currency conversion; 1 in 4 exchanges currency right before departure, which exposes them more to exchange rate fluctuations; 19% exchange currency online and then use their card for payments. Differences also emerge across generations. Young people (ages 18–29) use online currency exchange and card payments in foreign currency more often, while respondents between the ages of 45 and 65 prefer direct card payments and automatic currency conversion. Regardless of the methods used, the study’s data suggest that frequent use of foreign currency goes hand in hand with a higher level of financial organization: these respondents are more likely to have an emergency fund, health insurance, or to purchase travel insurance before departure. Not all Romanians pack travel insurance in their luggage Differences also emerge in how Romanians view travel insurance. One in five has never purchased such a policy, and the percentage rises among young people: 33% of those aged 18 to 29 say they have never sought this type of coverage. On the other hand, 42% purchase insurance every time they travel abroad, with those aged 45 to 65 being the most consistent: nearly half of them purchase insurance every time. The main reason Romanians do not always purchase travel insurance is not the cost, but a low perception of risk. One-third of respondents say they have not encountered serious problems while traveling and have managed without it, while 23% do not consider insurance necessary. Plan your vacation right from the banking app ING Current Account Packages include useful travel benefits tailored to each customer’s needs. ING Go covers everyday banking and includes favorable, 24/7 currency exchange rates for transactions of up to 10,000 lei per month. ING More retains this benefit and adds travel insurance for the account holder and their family, with coverage for medical emergencies, travel delays, lost or delayed luggage, civil liability, and roadside assistance. The package also includes 3 annual visits to business lounges in Romania, a 12% discount on BlackCab, and access to the Visa Luxury Hotel Collection. The benefits included have an estimated value of up to 470 lei, while the cost of the package is just 39 lei per month. For those who travel more frequently, ING Extra expands the benefits included in the More Package: the favorable currency exchange rate becomes unlimited, the included card is a Visa Platinum, access to business lounges in Romania increases to 6 visits per year, and the package adds Priority Pass with 4 free entries per year to international lounges, a 15% discount at BlackCab, and discounts at SIXT Rent A Car. The value of the included benefits can reach 920 lei, at a package cost of 220 lei per month. *The study was conducted in April 2026 on a sample of 1,051 respondents, urban residents, aged 18 to 65, who use banking products. The research is quantitative, primary, and ad hoc, with a maximum sampling error of ±3.0% at a 95% confidence level. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm74.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said in August it would not host Ye By Riyah Collins BBC Newsbeat Published 1 October 2026 Two stadium gigs in Russia by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, have officially been cancelled. West had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October. But there was confusion in the lead-up to the shows, as the venue had said it wouldn't host him for what would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. In a post on messaging app Telegram, gig organisers Say Agency confirmed the concerts had been cancelled with "sincere regret". "The Ye concerts in St Petersburg will not be able to take place on the scheduled dates," the Moscow-based agency wrote. "We will issue an official statement regarding the status of the project and our plans in the near future." Image source, Getty Images Image caption, West returned to touring earlier this year and has had a string of US stadium shows Gazprom Arena said in August that it had not signed a rental agreement with the concert promoters and so the gig could not take place on its site. Say Agency had said it was working to resolve the issue with the stadium before confirming they could not go ahead. The stadium also acknowledged it had received complaints about West's performance. He has recently apologised for multiple antisemitic and pro-Nazi comments in the past, saying he had "lost touch with reality" as a result of his bipolar disorder. Kanye West controversies - how did we get here? Published 7 April Kanye West concert in Poland cancelled over antisemitic comments Published 17 April Italy bans Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts over security concerns Published 30 May Russia was invaded by the Nazis in World War Two, and the country's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman was among those who criticised the planned shows. Maria Zakharova said they were unacceptable and pointed out West's "glorification" of Hitler. In 2025 West started selling swastika T-shirts and released a song called Heil Hitler. Pro-war bloggers in Russia also questioned whether the country should be hosting an American artist while the US provided financial and military support for Ukraine. West is yet to comment publicly on the cancellation. His first major concert in the US for more than five years was held in Los Angeles in April, and he has since played in countries including Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands. However, his Russian shows aren't the only gigs to have been cancelled. Last summer West was set to headline London's Wireless Festival but was barred from entering the UK, forcing organisers to cancel the whole event . West shows were also cancelled in Poland, Italy and France. Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here . https://www.mediafax.ro/english/calin-ge.text: Călin Georgescu detained by DIICOT in fraud case involving €1 million in damages On Monday, September 21, the DIICOT Central Structure, together with officers from the Criminal Investigation Directorate of the General Inspectorate of the Romanian Police (IGPR), carried out five home searches in Bucharest and the localities of Mogoșoaia, Ciolpani, and Buftea. The operation was part of an investigation into the formation of an organized crime group and fraud with particularly serious consequences, committed on a continuing basis. According to information released by DIICOT, the investigation targets three individuals—two Romanian citizens aged 64 and 47, and an Italian citizen aged 56—who allegedly formed an organized crime group in September 2021. Investigators allege that the group operated in Romania and the UK, with members posing as prosperous businessmen and administrators of foreign companies capable of facilitating significant financing from foreign banking institutions. Călin Georgescu, a former candidate in the 2024 presidential election, is mentioned in connection with this investigation.
